chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension and obesity with associated metabolic risk
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57‑year‑old woman with a long‑standing history of obesity (BMI ≥ 30 since 1986) and essential hypertension diagnosed in 2018. Recent vital signs show stage 2 hypertension (SBP 143 mmHg, DBP 105 mmHg) despite being on low‑dose lisinopril. She has prediabetes (A1c 5.9 %) and chronic musculoskeletal pain from knee osteoarthritis and low‑back pain, for which she uses naproxen regularly. Chronic anemia has been present since 2008 without a documented work‑up. Stress, limited transportation, and full‑time employment are noted as ongoing social stressors. No recent emergency or inpatient encounters have occurred; the last recorded visit was in May 2021, primarily for wellness care. Key laboratory data (lipids, renal function, BMI) are missing, limiting full risk assessment.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior dental disease (gingivitis, caries), a streptococcal sore throat treated in 2018, previous part‑time employment, limited social contact, and earlier medication review prompts. The patient also has a historical miscarriage in 1985. No chronic illnesses beyond those listed as active have been documented as resolved.

active_medications.name: naproxen sodium 220 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Pain control for osteoarthritis of the knee and chronic low back pain

social_determinants: Patient reports full‑time employment but has longstanding transport problems and lack of reliable transportation, which may limit access to care and healthy lifestyle resources. She also reports chronic stress. Educational attainment is higher education. No smoking or alcohol data are available.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure is in the stage 2 range (143/105 mmHg). Obesity is documented (BMI ≥ 30) though exact value is missing. Prediabetes (A1c 5.9 %) places her at risk for progression to type 2 diabetes. Comorbidity flags indicate hypertension, anemia, and osteoarthritis. Charlson comorbidity index is 1, indicating moderate clinical complexity. Polypharmacy risk is low (2 meds). Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (uncontrolled hypertension, obesity, prediabetes), renal (NSAID use with ACE‑inhibitor, no renal labs), metabolic (prediabetes, obesity), musculoskeletal (OA, chronic pain), hematologic (anemia), and psychosocial (stress, transportation barriers).

clinical_impression: A middle‑aged woman with uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes, compounded by chronic musculoskeletal pain and anemia. Social barriers (transportation, stress) and limited laboratory data hinder optimal risk stratification and management. She is at high cardiovascular risk and has potential renal vulnerability due to concurrent ACE‑inhibitor and NSAID use.
